audit_findings.message: No distribution events. Largest discrepancy on other days 0.000 bp; largest calendar-year drift 0.000 bp (smallest yearly tolerance 11.0 bp); cumulative drift +0.000 bp.

regression.caption: In-sample: uses the whole window (2010-01-04 to 2012-10-05, n = 720). Newey-West HAC standard errors with 6 lags, normal reference distribution. Betas are tagged reliable when significant after a Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the 5 betas (q = 0.05); alpha is a single test at 5%. Bars show the 95% interval for each beta on its own (not adjusted for multiple testing).
regression.alpha_sentence: Alpha of +4.80% a year cannot be told apart from zero: residual volatility is 19.30% a year over 2.9 years, so the standard error of annual alpha is 10.90%.

rolling.caption: Each point uses the previous 126 trading days, ending on that date (exactly 126 rows of the sample, HAC lags 4). The first 125 days have no estimate (warm-up).
Each point uses the previous 252 trading days, ending on that date (exactly 252 rows of the sample, HAC lags 4). The first 251 days have no estimate (warm-up).

average_beta.caption: Average of 469 overlapping 252-day estimates. The spread shows how exposure moved over time; it is not a standard error. The average of rolling betas generally differs from the full-sample beta.

return_contribution.caption: Annualised (x252) means over the sample, using full-sample betas. Alpha, the residual and the memo rows are shown separately; nothing is folded into alpha.
memo: Not covered by factor data: none (every analysed date has factor data).

risk_contribution.caption: Shares of variance over 2010-01-04 to 2012-10-05; they add to 100%.

residual_diagnostics.caption: Diagnostics of the full-sample regression residuals, each at a nominal 5% and not corrected for multiple testing. Only the lag-1 autocorrelation feeds the residual quality gate.
residual_diagnostics.lag1_reading: Lag-1 autocorrelation of the residuals is -0.04 (robust z -1.0). No clear day-to-day pattern.

tests.name: Ljung-Box
tests.reading: Ljung-Box (10 lags) does not reject no autocorrelation (p 0.780). It assumes constant variance, so it rejects too often on daily returns; read the robust test below.

tests.name: Robust Breusch-Godfrey
tests.reading: Autocorrelation test robust to changing volatility (10 lags): no autocorrelation detected (p 0.765).

tests.name: Jarque-Bera
tests.reading: Residual tails: consistent with a normal distribution (Jarque-Bera p 0.755, skew +0.07, excess kurtosis -0.0).

tests.name: Durbin-Watson
tests.reading: Durbin-Watson 2.07: near 2 means little first-order autocorrelation; above 2 points to negative, below 2 to positive autocorrelation.

residual_diagnostics.note: Standard errors are Newey-West HAC for every regression whatever these tests show; the tests are informational.

quality_gate.caption: Fires when the lag-1 autocorrelation of the residuals is below -0.2 and its robust z is below -4: part of each day's residual then reverses the next day, typical of closing prices that are not synchronous with the factor data. A pre-specified heuristic, applied to every ticker.

five_day_regression.reason: the residual quality gate did not fire
five_day_regression.caption: Sums of daily returns over non-overlapping blocks of 5 trading days, starting at the first day of the sample; same regression and Newey-West HAC errors as the daily one, alpha annualised as 252/5 times the block intercept. Computed because the residual quality gate fired: summing over 5 days lets most of a reversing price error cancel.

warnings.message: Only 720 daily observations (fewer than 750, about 3 years): estimates are imprecise.
Factor data ends 2012-10-05, 5157 days before the report date (the French library publishes with a lag of about a month). 0 later price days are not analysed.

notes: Every statistic is descriptive and in-sample, not predictive.
Uses the current Fama-French data vintage; historical factor values can be revised.

The factors are US Fama-French factors in USD. Applied to a non-US stock or a non-USD price series, betas mix factor exposure with currency and local-market effects. A ticker that Yahoo reports in another currency is refused; when Yahoo reports no currency, the ticker is analysed without that check.
Only tickers that exist today can be analysed. Results for survivors are not representative of companies that were delisted.

label_text.L-ARITH: Arithmetic contributions (not compounded); they add up exactly.
label_text.L-BAND: Pointwise 95% band. Even with a constant true beta, about 1 point in 20 falls outside.
label_text.L-OVERLAP: Overlapping windows: consecutive values share most of their data.
label_text.L-EXPL: Exploratory long-run link, not a trading signal.
label_text.L-PROXY: Return-based proxy, not a valuation spread.
label_text.L-VINTAGE: Uses the current Fama-French data vintage; historical factor values can be revised.
label_text.L-WORLD-PROXY: ACWI is the iShares MSCI ACWI ETF (an exchange-traded fund), used here as a stand-in for the MSCI ACWI index, which has no free daily data. It is priced in US dollars on a US exchange at the same close as US stocks.
label_text.L-WORLD-ASYNC: A quick estimate, not a full model. ACWI includes many non-US stocks (their share varies over time) whose markets close earlier than the US, so same-day co-movement with a US stock can be understated; this is not corrected here. A stock with a short history has a wide interval.
label_text.L-INSAMPLE: In-sample: betas are fitted on this same period.
label_text.L-PIT: Point-in-time: each day uses betas estimated only from earlier days.
label_text.L-HEDGE: Compounded daily: a paper long-short hedge, rebalanced daily, before trading costs, financing and borrowing fees.
label_text.L-KF: Kalman-filter beta: each point uses only data up to that date. It follows gradual changes smoothly, but reacts slowly to sudden changes; compare with the 126-day line. The drift rate is re-estimated once a year from past data, so the line can jump at those dates (marked).
label_text.L-KBAND: Model-based 95% band. It assumes normal, independent daily errors with constant variance and treats the estimated drift rate as known. It is not a Newey-West (HAC) interval and is not comparable to the rolling-beta bands. After a sudden change it is too narrow.
label_text.L-KTAIL: Daily price changes for this ticker partly reverse the next day (see the data-quality check). The filter ignores that, so the band is too narrow for this ticker.

world_beta.comparison_text: Higher against the world: the beta against the world is above the beta against the US market, and the two 95% intervals do not overlap.

residual.question: What did this stock return beyond its factor exposures, and does it hold up without hindsight?

in_sample.caption: Residual return = excess return minus factor exposures, alpha included. In-sample: betas fitted on 2010-01-04 to 2012-10-05, so the residual return equals the regression alpha exactly.

point_in_time.caption: Residual return with each day's betas estimated from the previous 252 trading days only. Covers 2010-12-22 to 2012-10-05; the first 252 days are warm-up.

gap.caption: Same days (2010-12-22 to 2012-10-05) for both series. Out-of-sample here refers to the betas; both series share the same days and stock-specific news.
gap.message: Neither residual return can be told apart from zero. Read both lines as noise.

chart.caption: Cumulative residual return, compounded daily. Both lines start at zero on 2010-12-21 and cover the same days. In-sample uses betas fitted on the whole period; point-in-time uses betas from the previous 252 days.

rolling_alpha.caption: Each point uses the previous 252 trading days, ending on that date; alpha and betas are both refitted in each window.

non_overlapping.caption: Separate one-year windows counted back from 2012-10-05. Corrected for testing 2 windows (Benjamini-Hochberg).

split_half.caption: One split, fixed in advance at the middle of the period. Betas are refitted in each half.

calendar_years.caption: Sum of daily residual returns within the year (not compounded). In-sample column: betas from the whole period. Point-in-time column: betas from the previous 252 days.

diagnostics.caption: Informational checks at the 5% level, not corrected for multiple testing.
findings: No clear day-to-day correlation in residual returns.
No clear departure from a normal distribution.
No clear clustering of residual volatility.

caveats: You see the stock's return after removing what its five factor exposures explain. It includes alpha.
In-sample: betas are fitted on this same period, so the in-sample line always drifts by the regression alpha. A line ending above zero is not evidence of skill; check the t-statistic.
Point-in-time: each day uses betas from the previous 252 trading days only. It removes hindsight in the betas, but it uses the same days, so it cannot rule out luck.
The lines compound a paper long-short hedge, rebalanced daily, before trading costs, financing and borrowing fees.
Past residual return does not predict future residual return.
